findings.evidence: “every entry this wizard newly registers gets an explicit `purpose`; absent `purpose` is reserved for a pre-migration entry” repeats the invariant already explained at lines 288–290 and 327–335 and in cli-model-selection.md lines 295–305.
findings.fix: Keep the detailed explanation of purpose capture in the selection steps and reduce Step 3 to a short instruction to carry each captured purpose into the JSON entry.

findings.evidence: “Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup or when ai-kit-spec-review warns no config exists” supplies clear triggers, but the description has no boundary distinguishing roster setup from running a review or configuring a host itself.
findings.fix: Configure ai-kit's cross-AI review and execute lanes in config.toml: detect installed CLIs and models, select runtime/model pairs and fallback order, check availability and stale providers, and migrate review-spec.toml. Use when users want reviewer or executor setup, availability checks, roster migration, or ai-kit-spec-review reports missing config. Default to .aikit/config.toml, announce the target, and ask before replacing an existing roster. Supports --check-only, --local and --global. Not for performing a review or execution task, configuring host providers, or managing credentials.

findings.evidence: The negative queries begin with “Write a unit test for the parser in the markdown-to-pdf skill” and otherwise cover unrelated documentation, Git, testing and status-line work; none tests a close boundary such as running an existing cross-AI review, configuring opencode providers, or editing runner retry settings. The positives also omit execute-lane setup.
findings.fix: Replace several unrelated negatives with realistic near-misses involving cross-AI review execution, host provider configuration, credentials and non-roster config tables; add positive queries for executor setup with casual and context-rich phrasing.

findings.evidence: The initial setup assertions check only “Runs detect-runtimes before asking any reviewer question” and “Runs check-providers after detection”; the remaining cases emphasize provider checks and gates rather than verifying the completed roster, purpose propagation, actual written ladder or trust consent.
findings.fix: Add an end-to-end output eval with verifiable assertions for review/execute purpose fields, the written fallback order, preservation of unrelated config, and explicit consent before trusting a command-bearing local roster. Add a rejected-entry warning case. This skill ships no runnable code under the supplied definition, so use the 8/7 allocation without scoring script tests.

findings.evidence: “probe-quota makes live probe calls to each configured CLI (same mechanism as dispatch time)” is followed by a cache/config-only explanation of “no writes.” This branch executes the probe without the write-risk consent that SKILL.md lines 253–260 require for unconfirmed read-only runtimes.
findings.fix: Before probing in --check-only, apply the same read-only capability check and explicit consent gate used for check-reviewer. Explain that cache isolation does not prevent a CLI from modifying the working tree; when consent is absent, skip the unsafe probe and report availability as unknown.

findings.evidence: “it always runs the full cfg_resolve merge” followed by “Report each key's available boolean only for keys that also appeared in the raw-read listing” filters by key alone. With --global, a local entry can override the same global key with a different runtime/model, so the reported availability can describe the local replacement rather than the requested global entry.
findings.fix: Match probe results to the effective entry identity, not only its key. When the merged entry differs from the raw target entry, report the target entry as unknown because it was shadowed, or use an existing read-only facility that probes the requested layer directly.
